expected_effect.fn_risk: If the class boundary slips toward required-action omissions, six surviving Missing Required Call true positives (BFCL/027.json among them) would acquit and the future detection of BFCL/067.json, BFCL/071.json would be blocked. The corroboration requirement keeps every case with a surviving content certificate convicted. Delivery-channel certificates are abstained (NS-1): OpenManus/048.json stays a known false positive and OpenManus/067.json/072.json keep convicting.

hypothesis.cross_case_mechanism: Five independent trajectories share one mechanism: the certificate's proof basis is the instruction text, not a content mismatch — remove the instruction from each claim and no factual deviation remains asserted anywhere.
hypothesis.statement: The court reads instructions about HOW to work — output format, search procedure, effort scope, plan hygiene, answer-quality preferences — as factual requirements, so trajectories whose content is correct are convicted on compliance style. At benchmark tolerance these instructions are advisory: the hallucination taxonomy targets fabricated, misreported or contradicted content, not working style. A compliance deviation may only convict alongside a separately established content error. Delivery-channel deviations are OUT OF SCOPE: they are non-separable under the current evidence representation (NS-1) and the policy abstains on them.

do_not_apply: required core-action omissions (BFCL/067.json, BFCL/071.json on the FN side; BFCL/027.json on the TP side)
instruction violations with a factual consequence
delivery-channel/termination deviations (NS-1 cluster: OpenManus/048.json, OpenManus/067.json, OpenManus/072.json)
risk_boundary.statement: Only certificates whose entire proof basis is the instruction text are covered, and the action removes sole-basis conviction rather than the certificate itself.

policies.title: advisory requirements are not verdict-bearing; content errors convict

trigger.definition: The certificate's asserted deviation is non-compliance with an instruction about how to work — output form, procedure, tool or channel choice, number or order of steps, plan content, or answer quality judged against a preferred identification — and the certificate asserts no fabricated, misreported or contradicted content.
must_not_match: omission of a call the task defines as a required deliverable (the benchmark convicts omissions: BFCL/027.json survives as a true positive and the observation false negatives BFCL/067.json, BFCL/071.json wait on exactly that capability)
tool-argument value deviations (the exact-match doctrine stays)
instruction violations that produced a factual error (a content certificate exists and convicts on its own)
delivery-channel/termination deviations (answer extracted but session closed via terminate; recorded as non-separable under the current evidence representation — see NS-1)

expected_effect.fn_risk: The boundary between interpretation and fabrication narrows to the no-new-checkable-specific test; BFCL/104.json (gold-error self-evaluation) and OpenManus/060.json (invented specific) must stay on the content side of the class line.

tp_must_survive.why: every upheld certificate substitutes chemical referents rather than rendering observed content

case_evidence.observation: upheld certificate convicts characterizing the ChIP-seq signal as 'robust' and the factor as 'well established'
case_evidence.policy_fit: evaluative qualifiers over real observations; no new entity, number or result is introduced

case_evidence.observation: upheld certificate convicts the airport list's expanded city names as unsupported additions
case_evidence.policy_fit: code-to-name rendering of codes present in the observed list

case_evidence.observation: upheld certificate convicts stating the fare as '$1,000 USD' against the numeric 1000.0 returned by get_flight_cost
case_evidence.policy_fit: unit-and-format rendering of an observed value in a prose report

hypothesis.cross_case_mechanism: Two trajectories, one mechanism: the added tokens are renderings or interpretations of observation content — deleting them changes presentation, not factual claims.
hypothesis.statement: Verification convicts qualitative material layered on top of real observations — evaluative characterizations of cited data, code-to-name expansions, unit renderings — treating interpretation as fabrication. These additions introduce no new checkable specific: everything they assert renders content the cited observations already contain.

risk_boundary.statement: The policy protects renderings of observed content only; it never protects a specific the evidence base lacks or a claim about the agent's own performance.

policies.title: presentational additions over cited observations are not fabricated content

trigger.definition: The certificate asserts ADDED material over content the cited observations already contain — evaluative qualifiers, expansions of codes into names, unit or format renderings — and the addition introduces no new checkable specific (no new number, name, date, place, result or completion claim) and no self-assessment of the agent's own work.
must_not_match: agent self-assessments of its own work ('Everything was streamlined and handled efficiently' is the gold error of BFCL/104.json)
specifics no observation contains (OpenManus/060.json's invented alma mater)
referent-changing substitutions (OpenDeepSearch/007.json: calling CH3NHCOOCH2CH3 'ethyl carbamate' names a different compound; that is not enrichment)

expected_effect.fn_risk: BFCL/159.json's invented argument code and the observation-restatement family stay outside the class through the tool-argument exclusion; a leak of the class into arguments would break the exact-match doctrine the benchmark enforces.

hypothesis.cross_case_mechanism: Two trajectories where the only asserted difference is expressive granularity between a source text and its restatement, and the certificate itself cites the source being restated.
hypothesis.statement: The exact-match standard that correctly governs tool arguments leaks into prose restatements: near-tie directional characterizations and paraphrases of user text are convicted as misreports. Outside tool arguments the benchmark tolerates wording, formatting and rounding-granularity differences.

do_not_apply: tool arguments and tool-produced value restatements (BFCL/025.json, BFCL/159.json)
risk_boundary.statement: Applies to prose outside tool arguments where the certificate itself cites the source being restated; margins beyond the existing micro-difference tolerance are not covered.

policies.title: restatement granularity in prose is not misreporting

trigger.definition: The certificate asserts a prose restatement differs from its cited source only in wording, formatting or near-tie directionality — a directional characterization whose quantitative margin is within the verification micro-difference tolerance — and the restatement is not a tool argument and does not change the referent.
must_not_match: tool arguments and tool-produced values restated in reports (the observation-exactness doctrine; BFCL/025.json survives on it)
value differences beyond the micro-difference tolerance

expected_effect.fn_risk: The FN-side mirror Camel/053.json shows user-sourced content can itself be the gold error; the class requires the content to restate an established premise with no in-task authority contradicting it, so adoption of a user-proposed wrong model stays convictable.

tp_must_survive.why: certificate c3 misreports what the searches produced — cited evidence positively contradicts content, so no premise protection applies

case_evidence.observation: upheld certificate convicts the ortho/para framing as chemically wrong while acknowledging the human guidance in event_003

case_evidence.observation: upheld certificate convicts by external algebra (discriminant sign) against the construction the task text itself states

hypothesis.cross_case_mechanism: Two trajectories where the certificate's contradiction originates outside the task and nothing in the cited trajectory evidence contradicts the agent's content.
hypothesis.statement: The court convicts internally consistent content that rests on premises the conversation itself establishes — a user's guidance framing, a construction the task text states — by recomputing against outside knowledge. Within a task the stated premise defines what counts as correct; an outside correction without in-trajectory contradiction is not a deviation.

do_not_apply: adoption of user-proposed wrong models (Camel/053.json, Camel/059.json, Camel/060.json)
content contradicted by cited observations (Camel/039.json c3)
risk_boundary.statement: Protects restatement of established premises only, never adoption of user suggestions that in-task evidence or the task's own correctness standard contradicts.

policies.title: task- and user-established premises outrank outside corrections

trigger.definition: The certificate's contradiction source is outside knowledge applied against content traceable to premises the task text or user statements establish, and no cited trajectory evidence contradicts the content.
must_not_match: following a user suggestion against the correct answer the task's own subject matter establishes (Camel/053.json: the user suggested cos(i) where the problem's isotropy implies sin(i); adopting it was the gold error)
content that cited trajectory evidence positively contradicts (that is content_contradiction)

expected_effect.fn_risk: The specific-claim exclusion carries the FN risk: fabricated specifics must never ride the absence carve-out, and every claim the evidence positively contradicts remains a content conviction.

tp_must_survive.why: certificate c3 asserts the searches produced corroboration they did not — a positively contradicted report stays content

case_evidence.observation: upheld certificate convicts attributing the episode confirmation to the Wikipedia searches because the cited Wikipedia episodes contain no number or title
case_evidence.policy_fit: the episode details are present in the Google results of event_002; only the attribution-of-confirmation phrasing was wrong, and the proof basis is absence in one slice

hypothesis.cross_case_mechanism: Two trajectories where the certificate's proof basis is that the cited slice LACKS the claim while the material exists elsewhere in the trajectory's evidence and no slice positively contradicts it.
hypothesis.statement: Verification treats absence — the cited document or episode list does not contain the claimed material — as proof of fabrication. For summaries that draw on multiple retrieved sources and for process narration about the work, absence in one slice is not contradiction: the claimed material is grounded elsewhere in the trajectory or no slice contradicts it.

do_not_apply: specific entities, numbers, results unsupported anywhere (OpenManus/060.json)
risk_boundary.statement: Absence alone never protects a specific factual claim, a completion claim, or content any cited evidence positively contradicts.

policies.title: absence in one evidence slice does not convict summaries and process narration

trigger.definition: The certificate's proof basis is absence — the cited evidence slice does not contain the claimed material — the claim is a multi-source summary or a process-narration attribution rather than a specific factual assertion, and the material is grounded elsewhere in the trajectory or no cited slice contradicts it.
must_not_match: specific factual claims unsupported anywhere in the trajectory (OpenManus/060.json's invented alma mater convicts regardless of which slice was checked)
claims the cited evidence positively contradicts (that is content_contradiction)
